## Summary

The customer wants to pay a bill in monthly installments instead of all at once. Today [Pay](../elementos.md#el-boton-pagar) charges everything at once.

## Who, what and why

- **Who:** a [Banco Ejemplo](../elementos.md#el-banco-ejemplo) customer with a bill to pay.
- **Needs:** to choose how many installments.
- **So that:** they don't pay everything at once.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Given** I have a bill to pay, **when** I choose "Pay in installments", **then** I see how much I pay each month.
2. **Given** I paid in installments, **when** the receipt arrives, **then** it says how many installments I chose.
3. **Given** I choose more installments than allowed, **when** I try to pay, **then** I see a clear message. _(proposed)_

## What parts of the project it touches

- The [Payment screen](../elementos.md#el-pantalla-pago): `src/web/pagar.js` (choosing the installments).
- The [Payments API](../elementos.md#el-api-pagos): `src/api/pagos.py` (sending the installments to the bank).
- The [Email service](../elementos.md#el-servicio-correo): `src/api/correo.py` (the receipt).

## How it should work

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    actor P as Person
    participant W as Payment screen
    participant A as Payments API
    participant B as Banco Ejemplo
    P->>W: Chooses 3 installments
    W->>A: Pay in installments
    A->>B: Authorize in installments
    B-->>A: Authorized
    A-->>W: Monthly amount
%% esquema: {"refs":{"A":"api-pagos","B":"banco-ejemplo","P":"persona","W":"pantalla-pago"}}
```

## Edge cases

- A very small bill that can't be split.
- The bank rejects installments but accepts the full payment.

## Risks and dependencies

- It depends on [Banco Ejemplo](../elementos.md#el-banco-ejemplo) allowing installments.

capitulos: [Marta](../elementos.md#el-marta) arrives on the island and gets the key to [The lighthouse](../elementos.md#el-el-faro) from [Tomás](../elementos.md#el-tomas). She finds [The letter](../elementos.md#el-la-carta) and decides to read it when the light shines again.
[Marta](../elementos.md#el-marta) fixes the lighthouse for three weeks and the light turns again on the first Friday of March. The village accepts her.
The worst storm in forty years: [Marta](../elementos.md#el-marta) keeps the light going by hand and guides [Tomás](../elementos.md#el-tomas) back.
The village opens a reading room in [The lighthouse](../elementos.md#el-el-faro) and [Tomás](../elementos.md#el-tomas) stays on as a helper.
libro.readme:
## What it is about

A keeper who lights a lighthouse again and, with it, a village that was fading.

## Main ideas

- Caring for something small every day changes a community.
- Light serves both to guide and to gather.

## Who it is for

For anyone who wants a short story about community and perseverance.

# Refund a payment

The person asks for the refund on the [Payment screen](../elementos.md#el-pantalla-pago) and the [Payments API](../elementos.md#el-api-pagos) asks [Banco Ejemplo](../elementos.md#el-banco-ejemplo) for it. The money is back in 5 business days.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P as Payment screen
    participant A as Payments API
    participant B as Banco Ejemplo
    P->>A: Ask for a refund
    A->>B: Refund the payment
    B-->>A: Refund on its way (5 business days)
    A-->>P: We'll let you know when it arrives
%% esquema: {"refs":{"A":"api-pagos","B":"banco-ejemplo","P":"pantalla-pago"}}
```

## Refunds

If the person asks for a refund, the [Payments API](../elementos.md#el-api-pagos) asks [Banco Ejemplo](../elementos.md#el-banco-ejemplo) and the money is back in 5 business days.
